body:
You put a lot into your Black Friday creative, and you want it to work as hard as possible. The question is how long it lasts. Ad platforms like Meta and Google now rely on the creative itself to find buyers, so the number of distinct ads a team can ship limits how much it can spend profitably.

In a live workshop on refreshing ads for Black Friday and Cyber Monday, Gabe Michael, forward deployed creative at ElevenLabs, and Jan Emmanuele, deployment strategist at ElevenLabs, walked through why creative production is the bottleneck in peak season and what an always-on alternative looks like. This post covers what they shared and how to apply it between now and January.

## Key takeaways

• Creative is the targeting. With broad targeting, platforms use your ads to find your audience, and near-identical ads count as one idea. Variety drives performance.

• Volume finds winners. Winning ads are rare and hard to predict, so the teams that test the most creative find them most often.

• Peak season punishes repetition. Spend concentrates into a few days, frequency climbs, and response drops with every repeat view.

• Your best ad is your most valuable asset. Extend it with new hooks, voices, music, and languages before you build something new.

• The handoff is the bottleneck. A workflow built on sequential handoffs can't refresh weekly. A loop that reads performance and generates variants can.

## Creative became the constraint

Targeting on ad platforms has become much broader. Instead of narrow audience settings doing the work, the platforms read the ad and decide who should see it. That changes what a creative team is for. Ads that look and sound nearly the same get treated as a single idea, so 10 slight tweaks of one concept buy you very little new reach or insight.

Winning ads are rare and hard to predict. A team shipping a few new ads each week waits a long time between winners, while a team shipping many more finds them far sooner. That's why the strongest brands test far more creative than everyone else, and why the winner is often an ad nobody on the team would have picked.

## Why ads wear out faster in peak season

Peak season compresses all of this. A large share of November and December online spend lands in the five days of Cyber Week, and every brand is bidding for the same shoppers in that window. Your top ads will get seen, but they'll get seen by the same people over and over. With each repeat view, someone who hasn't already converted is less likely to act.

The weeks after launch are harder. Teams have to spot which ads are wearing out, replace them before results drop, and carry what worked into December and January.

## Localization is an underused lever

People respond better to ads in their own language. However, many teams still run in only one language, because in the past, each new language meant a new production cycle with its own budget and turnaround. The result is that a proven ad stays in one market, or brands take an original-language ad to other markets where it does not resonate as well.

As a result, brands either run their original-language ads globally and accept lower conversion rates in non-native markets, or they localize a handful of priority markets and ignore the long tail. Taking a winning ad into a new market is often cheaper than finding a new winner there. ElevenLabs' paid marketing team did this with its own ads .

## From production line to always-on engine

The traditional creative model runs in sequence: brand identity, creative strategy, production, distribution, then analysis at the end. Each step hands off to the next, and each handoff costs time many teams don't have during peak season. Adding AI usually replaces the production step with prompting, which speeds up one stage but keeps every handoff in place.

Michael and Emmanuele described a different model, where agents run every step and the team directs the work as creative producers. That's how Ads Engine in ElevenCreative is built. It started as an internal workflow for the ElevenLabs paid marketing team to localize campaigns across seven languages.

With Ads Engine, you can:

• Connect your ad accounts on TikTok, Google, Meta, and LinkedIn. The engine pulls in live ads and their performance data, so you start from what already works.

• Get a signal when a creative starts to fatigue, so you can refresh before results drop.

• Generate new variants , localized versions, and personalized versions, with brand and compliance rules carried through every asset.

• Review before anything goes live, with an optional approval workflow and optional review by native-speaker linguists

• Push approved ads back to your platforms. Results stream back in, and you can ask the agent which creative is fatiguing or which hook to test next.

## Demo: new sizes, variants, and languages for a static ad

Scenario: The team wants to turn a live Black Friday static ad into more sizes, variants, and languages before it fatigues.

• Generating 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, and 16:9 versions from a single asset, keeping fonts and colors on brand

• Changing the offer by typed instruction, for example updating the discount, call to action (CTA), or background image

• Generating new background imagery from the brand kit for visual variants

• Suggesting alternatives for the headline and CTA, read directly from the existing ad

• Re-theming the same ad from Black Friday to Christmas with new imagery and copy

• Translating selected variants in bulk, with optional review by native-speaker linguists trained on ad creative

Why it matters: Every variant in every language comes from one approved concept, without a new design or translation cycle for each.

## Demo: new hooks and dubbing for a video ad

Scenario: The team wants to refresh a live video ad with new hooks and take it into new markets.

• Generating new opening hooks in the same voice, with lip sync and on-screen captions updated to match

• Dubbing across languages
ar_body:
نشرت ElevenLabs ملخصًا لورشة مباشرة حول تجديد إعلانات الجمعة السوداء والاثنين الإلكتروني، قدّمها غيب مايكل وجان إيمانويل من فريق ElevenLabs. تشرح الورشة لماذا أصبح إنتاج المحتوى الإبداعي عنق الزجاجة في موسم الذروة، وكيف يبدو البديل المستمر.

• المحتوى الإبداعي أصبح هو الاستهداف: منصات مثل Meta وGoogle تستخدم الإعلان نفسه لإيجاد الجمهور، والإعلانات المتشابهة تُحسب فكرة واحدة.

• الكمية تكشف الإعلانات الفائزة: الإعلانات الناجحة نادرة ويصعب توقعها، لذا الفرق التي تختبر أكثر تجدها أسرع.

• موسم الذروة يعاقب التكرار: ينصبّ جزء كبير من الإنفاق في أيام قليلة، فيرتفع التكرار وتنخفض الاستجابة مع كل مشاهدة.

• أفضل إعلان هو أثمن أصولك: مدّه بخطافات وأصوات وموسيقى ولغات جديدة قبل بناء إعلان جديد.

• التسليم المتسلسل بين الفرق هو العائق، أما حلقة تقرأ الأداء وتولّد نسخًا جديدة فتسمح بالتجديد الأسبوعي.

توضح المقالة أن الفرق التي تنتج تنوعًا أكبر من الإعلانات تحقق أداءً أفضل في موسم التسوق المزدحم.
